content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (preferred-level cure proposed).**

- **What exists:** §14.2(B) gives us an M&I indemnity that expressly covers third-party claims that the Services or M&I software infringe US patents, copyrights or trademarks, and §14.3 supplies the full procedure (notice, assumption/control of defence with reasonably satisfactory counsel, full cooperation). So the rule is not "missing," and the IP core and procedural elements are already met.
- **Why it still fails the checklist:** M&I's indemnity runs only to Customer (not affiliates) and omits M&I's violation of applicable law generally (only protected-class statutes are listed), M&I-caused unauthorized access to or disclosure of our data, and M&I's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Conversely, our own §14.2(A) indemnity is sweeping — representations/warranties, protected-class laws, harassment, work-related injury, all property/financial loss from our acts or omissions, plus §6.6(B) matters — far beyond Customer-provided content and our own breach of law.
- **Cure (two surgical ops):** a new Paragraph C extending Paragraph B's indemnity/defence to our affiliates and the three missing conduct categories, and a narrowing of the §14.2(A) list to Customer-supplied content/data/materials and Customer's violation of applicable law. Lowercase "applicable law" was used deliberately, since the defined "Applicable Law" is limited to ACH/NACHA rules.
- **Not double-flagged:** §13.4's three-month liability cap (which would swallow any indemnity) is a limitation-of-liability issue; I noted it in the rationale rather than importing the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap or adding Vendor-favourable IP exclusions.
